QS.q: Why does this exist? What problem goes away?
Drill past the stated purpose to the real need.
What is this deliberately NOT doing?
Who benefits, and how would they notice?
How do we know it worked? A measurable test, not a feeling.
Who has to agree to this — and who could block it?
Who owns it? Who answers for it?
Who runs it day to day? Who gets the 3am call?
What happens to whom when it fails? Who gets hurt?
Who pays to build it, run it, and maintain it?
How does this make money, save money, reduce risk, or create opportunity — and what does doing nothing cost?
QS.hint: Also: why would whoever pays keep paying? What happens if the problem is simply ignored? For a personal build, the currency is your time, reputation or opportunity — not just money.

QS.q: What else solves this today — rival products, existing tools, a manual workaround, or doing nothing? Why would anyone pick this instead?
QS.hint: Include buy vs build: could you buy, borrow or reuse something rather than build it? In a contest — a bid, a pitch, a hiring round — the competition is the other entries: what makes yours the one they pick?

QS.q: What can't change? Budget, time, rules, hardware, skills.
What data does it touch? Is any of it personal or regulated (GDPR, FCA, etc.)?
What do we rely on that we don't control? APIs, providers, libraries, people.
How big does it get? What breaks at 10x?
What are 2–3 ways to build it — or buy, borrow or reuse it instead?
Why this one over the others? What are we giving up?
Commit. What did you choose, what did you reject, and what are you accepting?
What's the smallest version worth shipping first? What comes after?
What must be true for this choice to hold?
How do we know the assumptions hold?
How do we see problems happening?
What breaks first — and what's the first failure that does real damage?
QS.hint: They aren't always the same. The first thing to break may be harmless; the first thing that costs money, customers, trust or the deal is the one to design for.

QS.q: Drill from the failure to the thing that actually caused it.
Who could abuse this, and what's the worst they could do?
How do we get back to working — and fix the root cause, not just the symptom?
Once it's live, how do changes get proposed, approved, and recorded?
What happens if I disappear?
Can a stranger understand it and change it?
What's the kill signal — the checkable condition that means stop — and what happens then?
QS.hint: Decide it now, while stopping is cheap. Once you've sunk time in, every signal looks like a reason to keep going.

QS.q: Export this, hand it to someone else or a fresh AI, and ask them to attack it. What did they find, and what are you changing?

MODES: Curiosity, learning, a toy or a weekend build. Keep it light.
Proving a technique, library or approach actually works.
A real system someone will depend on, pay for or judge.

FUNQ.PURPOSE: What's the itch? What makes this interesting enough to spend time on?
FUNQ.SUCCESS: What would make this feel worth the time — something you learn, see work, or can show someone?
FUNQ.CONSTRAINTS: How much time are you giving it, and what's off-limits (money, tools, scope)?
FUNQ.FIRST SLICE: What's the smallest version that would be fun to see working?
FUNQ.FAILURE: What's most likely to stall it — or make you lose interest?
FUNQ.RETIREMENT: What tells you to stop — and is it done, shelved, or promoted to a real project?

JMODES: Small builds, or a first look at any idea. 10 fixed steps.
Anything with impact above annoying, or with money or other people.
A business idea. Your business rules apply.
A personal or career decision. Your career rules apply.

FCODES.F4: No success test, or no date
FCODES.F5: A stranger can't see it run
FCODES.F6: Costs left out of the numbers
FCODES.F7: Other people's money, data or keys
FCODES.F9: Only self-validated: James believes it, builds it, and judges it

VERDICTS: Go. Needs a first slice and a date.
Good idea, wrong time. Parked on purpose, with a revisit trigger.
